newsitem.title: GERMANY: France not to ease budget pact, Delors tells paper.
newsitem.headline: France not to ease budget pact, Delors tells paper.

text.p: Former European Union President Jacques Delors said France had no desire to water down the so-called "stability pact" protecting the euro and warned against delaying the single currency project.
Delors told the newspaper Die Zeit it was "absolutely vital" to stick to the timetable for monetary union and that the single currency would make Europe's economy more dynamic.
The former EU leader also said he did not believe that French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin wanted to water down the "stability pact" to ensure fiscal discipline after the introduction of the euro.
"Lionel Jospin made clear during the political campaign he wants to implement the Treaty for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), nothing but the contract and the whole contract," Delors said.
Die Zeit provided a copy of the article to the media before its official publication on Thursday.
Delors said Jospin's desire to see Europe create a body of economic advisors that could act as a political counterweight to the European Central Bank was not an attack on the stability pact.

He said the Maastricht Treaty already foresaw European heads of state making recommendations on economic policy and that this provision should be made into a protocol which could be added to the stability pact.
Jospin was swept to power in French elections on Sunday and campaigned on the promise of more jobs and a stronger economy.
